indication_tracked: Adjuvant treatment after complete tumour resection in adults with ALK-positive NSCLC at high risk of recurrence

eu.jca_note: No EU Joint Clinical Assessment: this indication was authorised before the EU HTA Regulation applied (12 January 2025).
eu.epar_summary:
Alecensa is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is only used when the cancer is ‘ALK-positive’, which means that cancer cells have changes in the gene that makes a protein called anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK).

Alecensa is used on its own in adults with:
• advanced NSCLC that has never been treated before or has already been treated with a cancer medicine called Xalkori (crizotinib);
• NSCLC that has been removed by surgery (adjuvant treatment) and is at high risk of coming back.

Alecensa contains the active substance alectinib.
eu.epar_summary_note: Copied word for word from the Overview section of the EMA Alecensa page (EPAR medicine overview EMA/220238/2024, last updated 19/06/2024). Only the bullet marks were added.

DE.opinion: Population a) eligible for adjuvant platinum chemotherapy: indication of a considerable added benefit (Anhaltspunkt für einen erheblichen Zusatznutzen). Population b) after or unsuitable for platinum chemotherapy: added benefit not proven.
DE.comparator: a) Cisplatin + vinorelbine or cisplatin + pemetrexed; b) watchful waiting
